title: Procurement playbook sprint - prioritization & risk matrix

Pricing path for pilot to committed capacity
Technical preflight for private VPC deployment

Marcus Liu (Novus) — provide representative traffic profile and peak concurrency windows for store search API by 2025-10-28
Aisha Khan (Novus Legal) — flag any non-negotiable DPA clauses and required data residency language by 2025-11-03
Ellen Park (Security) — confirm required certs (SOC 2 type II / ISO27001) and whether audit reports can be shared by 2025-11-07

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-23 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Platform: Zoom (recording: internal link)
Attendees: Liam O'Connell (Redwood AE); Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Jordan Reyes (Novus - Procurement); Aisha Khan (Novus - Counsel); Marcus Liu (Novus - Platform Eng); Ellen Park (Novus - Security); Samir Patel (Novus - FinOps)

Summary (auto): Align procurement and legal checklist; prioritize MSA/DPA items; identify technical preflight requirements for pilot.

00:00 Liam O'Connell: okay everyone thanks for hopping on, we'll try to keep this to an hour, we've got a packed agenda so i'll hand it to priya for the quick technical preface — priya?
00:18 Priya Shah: yeah thanks liam um hi team, quick context, we ran the basic latency profiles on our hosted runtime last month and saw p95 around 420 ms for a 512 token seq with our standard batching, that shifts with quantized model variants but i want to align on what your store-facing SLA expectation is so we can recommend dedicated or private bits
00:40 Jordan Reyes: yeah that's helpful, store search has to be snappy — users expect < 300 ms for the search path, but for async generative tasks it's fine to be higher. procurement is concerned about uptime windows and credits, we need to see what you consider a production SLA.
01:02 Priya Shah: understood, and just to flag there are tradeoffs — hitting 300 ms consistently may push you to dedicated GPU pools or lower batch sizes which affects unit cost. i'll show the three knobs in a sec.
01:20 Aisha Khan: can i interrupt — before we go deep technical, legally we need to understand data residency; some customer PII flows through the search logs, we need the DPA to guarantee EU residency for EU stores and to describe data retention and deletion paths. also K M S integration — do you support customer-managed keys?
01:42 Liam O'Connell: yep, great callouts. we support customer KMS in our Private offering, there's a managed KMS in hosted but for Novus compliance we can run customer KMS via bring-your-own-key in the VPC/private deployment. we'll detail that in the DPA appendix.
01:58 Marcus Liu: quick nit — does BYOK mean HSM support and can we leverage our existing cloud HSM? we prefer to manage rotation and have audit hooks.
02:12 Priya Shah: we have integrations with AWS KMS, Google KMS, and customer HSMs via a standard connector; rotation can be orchestrated from your side; audit logs are exportable to your SIEM. sometimes the transcriber says we have exportable logs, but the exact path depends on whether it's dedicated or private.
02:34 Ellen Park: also SOC 2 evidence — do you share attestation and do you have an ISO cert? security wants to see the report or a SOC letter.
02:44 Liam O'Connell: yes we can share SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 attestation under NDA; we'll include that as part of the security packet to Aisha and Ellen.
03:00 Jordan Reyes: procurement question on pricing — for the pilot, do you recommend a usage-first approach or committed reserved capacity? we have a six-week initial pilot across 200 stores and are worried about cost spikes.
03:18 Priya Shah: typical pattern is usage-based for the pilot, move to a small reserved commit if you want predictable unit cost. we can provide a pilot price sheet that models expected token volume plus a cap for egress/egress-ish fees.
03:35 Samir Patel: egress fees — we need clarity on egress out of regions, since we have EU and NA stores. are there cross-region charges between model hosting and store data?
03:50 Liam O'Connell: good question. we can pin region for inference, route EU traffic to EU region; if you use cross-region storage or replication there may be transfer fees but they're itemized. we'll add region egress examples to the pricing sheet.
04:08 Aisha Khan: on MSA redlines: our standard asks for flowdown of liability caps for data breach incidents and a clause for audit rights. can you accept limited carveouts for audit access? also we prefer a 60-day notice for major SLA changes.
04:28 Liam O'Connell: ballpark, our standard MSA has a liability cap tied to fees paid in 12 months; we can discuss exceptions. for audit rights we typically provide SOC 2 docs; if you need on-site audits that's a bigger lift. 60-day notice for SLA changes is reasonable to aim for.
04:45 Priya Shah: back to tech: three configurations to consider — hosted multi-tenant with our standard model (best $/token), dedicated reserved pool (predictable latency and throughput), private VPC (max isolation and BYOK). for sub-300 ms p95 we usually recommend dedicated with autoscale tuned to your peak concurrency.
05:10 Marcus Liu: if we go dedicated, can we pin kernel/quantization profiles? we have some custom model variants in our stack.
05:22 Priya Shah: yes you can pin model versions and quantization options in Dedicated; private allows even more control. note that custom kernels require validation — if it's an open model variant we have a onboarding path.
05:40 Jordan Reyes: ok procurement wise our priorities for the playbook sprint are: 1) clearly defined SLA thresholds and remedies, 2) DPA and residency language, 3) price-path for pilot to commit, 4) security attestations and KMS approach.
05:58 Liam O'Connell: great, let's map owners — we'll send an annotated MSA with two SLA options: A (99.9% uptime, credit ladder X) and B (99.95% with smaller credit but requires commit).
06:12 Aisha Khan: please include a force majeure carveout that's standard, and a clear incident response time commitment, not just detection time. we want time-to-notify and time-to-remediate expectations.
06:30 Priya Shah: we can add incident response SLOs — page-level: detect in 5 minutes, respond within 30, remediation targets vary by incident severity. those are examples, we'll formalize.
06:48 Samir Patel: about pricing, can you share an example of reserved vs usage for a 6-week pilot at expected QPS? we can plug numbers into FinOps models.
07:02 Priya Shah: i'll produce a matrix with p50/p95 numbers and token cost per 1000 tokens across hosted/dedicated/private for your traffic estimates.
07:16 Jordan Reyes: timeline — procurement needs vendor selection memo by 2025-11-10 to make this quarter's board cutoff. can redlines be concluded before then?
07:28 Liam O'Connell: yes that's doable if we get your redline priorities this week; we'll aim for MSA redline exchange by 2025-10-30 and a legal sync the week of 2025-11-03.
07:42 Ellen Park: on data deletion — we need confirmation of deletion APIs and ability to run deletion requests in bulk per region. are deletion timestamps and proof-of-deletion logs available?
07:56 Priya Shah: deletion APIs exist for Private and Dedicated; for hosted multi-tenant there are retention policies and purge flows. proof-of-deletion logs can be exported to your bucket as part of the compliance package. we'll include that in the DPA appendix.
08:12 Marcus Liu: technical question — does Redwood support prefix/KV cache warming between rollouts? we have a lot of cold starts when we swap models.
08:22 Priya Shah: yes we have KV cache prewarm hooks and warmup strategies; we can prepopulate caches for canary rollouts to avoid latency spikes. some of the transcribed notes might say KV cash but it's KV cache.
08:36 Jordan Reyes: if we need an enterprise-only clause around data not being used for model training, what's the process? we need a clear opt-out in the DPA.
08:48 Liam O'Connell: we do provide a no-training clause in enterprise contracts and can add that to the DPA; by default hosted telemetry may be used for quality but enterprise/private can opt out. we'll surface language.
09:04 Aisha Khan: liability cap — can we get a separate carveout for willful misconduct and gross negligence? that's standard for us.
09:16 Liam O'Connell: yes, carveouts for willful misconduct and gross negligence are typically excluded from the cap — standard practice. we'll mark that in the redline.
09:30 Samir Patel: one more on billing: do you support invoiced monthly with net-30? and any early-pay discounts?
09:40 Liam O'Connell: net-30 invoicing is supported for enterprise deals; early-pay discounts can be discussed for multi-year commits. we'll have finance follow up.
09:50 Jordan Reyes: procurement also asks about subcontractor flowdown — if Redwood uses a partner for model hosting, do you flow down DPA obligations to them?
10:04 Priya Shah: we require subprocessors to be bound by equivalent security obligations; the DPA appendix lists subprocessors and we can commit to notify you of changes.
10:18 Marcus Liu: regarding pilot data, we will provide a sample staging dataset with anonymized PII. how do we get that loaded to your staging endpoint?
10:30 Priya Shah: we'll create a staging workspace in the EU region, provide a secure upload link or SFTP depending on your preference, and run the synthetic pilot. i'll coordinate with marcus on the upload method.
10:46 Jordan Reyes: okay let's talk escalation paths — procurement wants a named Redwood contact for operational incidents and an engineering escalation ladder.
10:56 Liam O'Connell: that's me for commercial escalation, priya is technical lead, and we can include an on-call pager or Slack rotation for incidents above Sev 2. we'll include names and SLAs in the runbook.
11:10 Aisha Khan: do you have a standard mutual NDA or do we need to sign something before you send SOC docs?
11:18 Liam O'Connell: we can do mutual NDA; however SOC artifacts are often shared under a one-way NDA and MSA confidentiality clauses. we'll propose an NDA template if needed.
11:30 Priya Shah: quick note on rollback — we support automatic fallback to a lower-latency model variant if a rollout causes p95 regression; that can be part of the release policy in the runbook.
11:44 Ellen Park: curious about RBAC — can you map role-level permissions to our identity provider and limit access to production keys?
11:56 Priya Shah: yes we support SAML/SSO with SCIM provisioning; RBAC roles can be mapped and production keys restricted. we'll include an RBAC mapping template.
12:12 Jordan Reyes: wrapping — looks like strong alignment. procurement wants the MSA redline and SLA options by 10/30, legal wants DPA draft and security packet, SE to run pilot matrix next week. any other blockers?
12:30 Marcus Liu: none from platform, just need the upload instructions.
12:36 Samir Patel: finance will review the pricing matrix once it's in.
12:40 Liam O'Connell: great — recap and next steps: we'll send annotated MSA + two SLA tables, SE runs pilot and sends benchmark deck, security packet (SOC2/ISO) under NDA, and schedule legal redline review week of 11/03. thanks everyone.
12:56 Jordan Reyes: thanks all.
13:02 Aisha Khan: thanks liam, bye.
